events.title: Thomas Cranmer burned at the stake
events.description: In Oxford, Thomas Cranmer, Archbishop of Canterbury, was executed by burning during the reign of the Catholic queen Mary I. He had helped lead the English Reformation and shaped the Book of Common Prayer.
events.significance: His death made him one of the best-known Protestant martyrs of the English Reformation. It also showed how bitter the religious conflict in Tudor England had become.

events.title: The Napoleonic Code becomes French law
events.description: France adopted its civil code, soon known as the Code Napoléon. It replaced a patchwork of regional and feudal laws with a single legal system.
events.significance: The code stressed legal equality and property rights. It influenced legal systems across Europe, Latin America and beyond, and parts of it are still in use today.

events.title: Selma to Montgomery march begins
events.description: Martin Luther King Jr. led about 3,200 marchers out of Selma, Alabama, on the third attempt at the march. The first attempt had ended in violence on Bloody Sunday. This time the marchers had federal protection.
events.significance: The march drew national attention to the fight for Black voting rights. It helped build support for the Voting Rights Act of 1965.

events.title: The first tweet is sent
events.description: Twitter co-founder Jack Dorsey posted the first message on the new microblogging service.
events.significance: Twitter grew into a major platform for news, politics and public conversation. It changed how people share information in real time.
